function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** is a formal authorization that gives one party (the *mandator*) the right to act on behalf of another party (the *mandatee*). In practice it’s a contract‑based delegation of authority that can cover a wide range of activities—from signing documents to making investment decisions. ### Key points | Aspect | Explanation | |--------|-------------| | **Legal nature** | A written or verbal agreement that specifies the scope, limits, and duration of the authority granted. | | **Common contexts** | • **Finance & banking** – a client authorizes a bank or broker to trade securities, manage accounts, or execute payments.
• **Corporate governance** – a board delegates decision‑making to a committee or executive.
• **Government** – a minister delegates powers to a department or agency. | | **Typical components** | • Parties involved (mandator & mandatary)
• Scope of authority (what actions may be taken)
• Duration (time frame or conditions for termination)
• Conditions & limitations (e.g., maximum amounts, reporting requirements) | | **Status categories** | • **Active** – currently valid and enforceable.
• **Pending** – awaiting approval or execution.
• **Inactive** – expired, revoked, or otherwise no longer in effect. | ### Example in finance A private investor signs a *direct debit mandate* with a bank, allowing the bank to automatically withdraw monthly contributions from the investor’s account into a mutual fund. The mandate specifies: - The amount per withdrawal - The frequency (monthly) - The duration (until the investor cancels) If the investor later decides to stop the automatic withdrawals, they would send a cancellation notice, turning the mandate’s status to **inactive**. --- In short, a mandate is a legally binding instruction that empowers another party to act on your behalf within defined parameters.
